text: I see you're experiencing chest pain and shortness of breath; to help me understand the severity, can you describe exactly where the pain is located and what triggers it? Also, have you noticed any sweating, nausea, or pain radiating to your arm or jaw?

speaker: Patient
text: The pain feels like a tight band right in the center of my chest and it shoots down into my left arm and jaw. text: That sounds like classic angina; how long do these episodes typically last, and do they ever occur when you are at rest or during sleep? Also, do you have a history of high blood pressure, high cholesterol, or diabetes?

speaker: Patient
text: These episodes usually last about five to ten minutes and always seem to happen when I'm working hard or climbing stairs; they never bother me when I'm resting or sleeping. Yes, I've been dealing with high blood pressure for ten years and have high cholesterol, but I don't have diabetes.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Stable Angina Pectoris. Given your history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, along with exertional chest pain radiating to the jaw and arm, this is highly suggestive of coronary artery disease. I recommend an Electrocardiogram (ECG) and a Lipid Panel to assess your current cardiac status and cholesterol levels.
